chunks: And from him (Al-Hadhdha' or the previous narrator) from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him)
Like that (i.e., the same ruling previously mentioned).

key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ: Ali ibn Ja'far, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Musa (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Musa al-Kazim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the brother of Ali ibn Ja'far regarding Ihram expiation?
ai.summary: This concise hadith, transmitted through the prominent Banu Hashim lineage of Ali ibn Ja'far and Musa al-Imam, serves as a textual anchor within Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, confirming the consistency of the expiation (*kaffarah*) rulings for unintentional breaches of Ihram conditions. By referencing a prior narration, it underscores the jurisprudential principle that minor deviations from ritual boundaries require specific compensatory acts, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual purity and obligation.
